newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada July farm input price index up 1.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada July farm input price index up 1.3 pct.

text.p: Canada's farmers paid only 1.3 percent more to do business in the second quarter of 1997 compared with a year earlier, Statistics Canada said on Tuesday.
It was the lowest annual increase in almost five years.
The farm input price index rose to 130.7 (1986=100), after a 1.8 percent year-on-year rise registered in the first quarter.
Farmers in the West paid 2.1 percent more for their inputs -- the result of massively higher feeder cattle prices -- while in the East prices rose a marginal 0.5 percent.
Nationally, a 15.9 percent decline in the cost of interest helped offset a 39.2 percent rise in the price of feeder cattle and more expensive machinery and motor vehicles.
